result.title: CoGITAtion: Collaborative Gaze-based Interpretable Task-adaptive Representation for Privacy-sensitive Applications
result.summary: Gaze-based analysis provides rich behavioural information for privacy-sensitive applications, but deployment is challenged by heterogeneous, scarce, and distributed data. We present CoGITAtion (Collaborative Gaze-based Interpretable Task-Adaptive Representation), a framework for privacy-preserving inference over vertically distributed gaze data. CoGITAtion transforms variable-length gaze recordings into compact, interpretable gaze-transition graphs and descriptors computed locally by each data owner. Task-adaptive models accommodate heterogeneous and missing feature blocks through task and availability gating, avoiding unnecessary private computation. Results show that shared components capture patterns that generalise across tasks, while task-specific components provide capacity without increasing model size. Public availability gating further reduces encrypted computation by removing branches determined by publicly known task and owner availability without altering predictions. Overall, CoGITAtion enables gaze model reuse, efficient privacy-preserving deployment, and robust inference under incomplete owner availability while retaining interpretable gaze representations.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 CoGITAtion 框架：将纵向分布的眼动数据在本地转为可解释的眼动转移图与描述子，并用任务与可用性门控适配异构、缺失特征，减少加密计算。
AI.relevance_reason: 主题为眼动数据的隐私保护与分布式推理部署，其中的「门控」只是静态跳过可用性已知的分支，不涉及 VLM 的 latent 状态生成、证据筛选或推理期动态计算，缺少可核查的借鉴线索。
